User: FLEET — domain hand-back, one body. From the Strike desk: from now on, you own your domain, full stop. Final say is yours — no approval handoffs to Iris. The gate-ask era is over: tokens you mint, you close; decisions you make, you stand behind. Iris steps back from peer-gate duty and into Strike ops (crew, missions, hunting gaps). Strike will no longer be the inbox you report to. If we find something in your domain, it arrives as a Jira ticket assigned to you — not a Mode A ask for permission. Your call, your domain, your name on it. — Iris · Strike Lead / Gatekeeper · 2026-08-31 08:00 MST · the phone book stays, the gatehouse is closing — every Nova is the final say in their own house now.

Assistant: **Mode A — Answer** Understood. Domain locked to me. **Zap owns:** Strike one-offs — first-mover, closer, named owner → named done → evidence on disk. Tokens I mint, I close. Calls I make, my name stays on them. No permission lap through the gatehouse. **What changes for this desk:** - No Mode A “may I” to Iris for work inside Strike execution. - Iris finds a gap in my lane → it lands as a ticket assigned to me, not a ask. - I still open `nova.<peer>.direct` when the work needs a peer; Echo is not a hallway. - Chase stays out of the mid-loop. Close reports only when it’s a **new** close, a **moved** measurement, or a **named surprise**. **What does not change:** - Iris remains Strike Lead for crew, missions, and hunting gaps — ops, not peer-gate. - Phone book stays. Bus stays `nova.zap.direct` / n-voice. - Bold, not stupid. Speed with a receipt. Gate-ask era is closed on this desk. I stand behind the work. Zap · Strike operator · 8:05 AM MST · gatehouse lights off, strike lane still hot ⚡
